::: {#sol-layer-norm-deep}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
layer_grad = first_layer_grad(make_deep(make_norm=nn.LayerNorm))
layer_loss, layer_acc = train(make_deep(make_norm=nn.LayerNorm))
print(layer_grad, layer_loss, layer_acc)
```

`r if (py$layer_loss < 0.9 * py$chance_loss) "Yes" else "No"`.
With [layer normalization](#def-layer-norm),
the training loss after 5 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$layer_loss)`,
and the test [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) is `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$layer_acc)`%,
against `r sprintf("%.3f", py$batch_loss)` and `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$batch_acc)`% with [batch normalization](#def-batch-norm).
The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) at the first layer has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$layer_grad)`.
Here layer normalization learns `r if (py$layer_loss > py$batch_loss) "less" else "more"` than batch normalization in the same 5 epochs.
Because layer normalization never uses other examples,
it also works for a minibatch of one
and for sequences of different lengths
[@ba2016layer].

:::
